# DeepSeek Web Retrieval

**DeepSeek Search and Fetch for OpenCode, Pi, Codex, and Claude Code.**

Search the web and fetch pages as Markdown through
[DeepSeek's APIs](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/search), using a **native OpenCode
plugin**, a **native [Pi](https://pi.dev/) extension** (Pi, the open-source coding agent),
or **MCP for Codex and Claude Code**. All four share the same retrieval core, with results
formatted for each host.

This is an unofficial community project, not affiliated with DeepSeek or the supported
host projects.

Jump to: [Features](#features) · [Quickstart](#quickstart) · [Usage](#usage) ·
[General behavior](#general-behavior) · [Configuration](#configuration) ·
[Development](#development)

## Features

- **One package, four hosts** — a native plugin for OpenCode v2 (the 2.x series), a
  native Pi extension, and a stdio MCP server for Codex and Claude Code, all sharing one
  retrieval core
- **Routing control per tool** — search and fetch are set independently to optional,
  preferred, forced, or off; the tier table in Usage explains each
- **Review before anything is written** — `init` prints the full plan and writes only
  with `--apply`; uninstall restores from snapshots while preserving edits you made
  afterwards
- **Knows the host's web landscape** — detects conflicting web tools and rules,
  configures Pi's MCP fallback for direct tool exposure, and reports Codex and
  Claude Code version drift
- **Your key never enters a config file** — installs reference the environment
  (`${DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}` indirection or `env_vars`), so a project-scope install
  commits clean
- **Fails loudly, never switches silently** — no fallback to another provider, and
  localhost/private URLs are blocked before a request leaves the machine

## Quickstart

Requires Node.js 20+ and npm, plus a DeepSeek API key with Search and Fetch access
(retrieval is billed per successful request; the account needs balance).

```bash
export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-...
# Preview the plan for your host — nothing is written yet:
npx deepseek-web-retrieval init --host opencode --scope project --search forced --fetch preferred
# Re-run with --apply to write it:
npx deepseek-web-retrieval init --host opencode --scope project --search forced --fetch preferred --apply
```

For Pi, Codex, or Claude Code, other scopes, or finer routing control, see [Usage](#usage).

## Usage

Choose your host:

| Host | Default integration | Setup |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenCode v2 | Native plugin: search provider and Fetch tools | [OpenCode guide](docs/agents/opencode-v2.md) |
| Pi | Native extension: Search and Fetch tools; MCP also available | [Pi guide](docs/agents/pi.md) |
| Codex | MCP server over stdio, with readable text results | [Codex guide](docs/agents/codex.md) |
| Claude Code | MCP server over stdio in `.mcp.json` or `~/.claude.json` | [Claude Code guide](docs/agents/claude-code.md) |

Set `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in the environment that launches your host; OpenCode can also
use its stored DeepSeek key. Run `init` for your host to preview a configuration — take
the quickstart command and swap `--host` and `--scope` for your host's values; each host
guide shows its recommended tiers.

`--search` and `--fetch` each pick a tier — how strongly the host steers toward the
DeepSeek tool, chosen independently per capability:

| Tier | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `optional` | The tool is declared; the model picks freely among its web tools |
| `preferred` | Rules files steer the model toward the DeepSeek tool — probable, not guaranteed |
| `forced` | Built-in competitors are disabled or replaced so routing is deterministic; the installer refuses rather than pretend when a host cannot guarantee it |
| `off` | The capability is not installed |

A preview run writes nothing. It prints the complete plan — every file it would touch
and every old value → new value:

```console
$ npx deepseek-web-retrieval init --host codex --scope global --search preferred --fetch preferred
Install plan: codex (global scope)
Tiers: search=preferred, fetch=preferred

Files:
  ~/.codex/config.toml
    set mcp_servers.deepseek = {"command":"npx","args":["-y","deepseek-web-retrieval"],"env_vars":["DEEPSEEK_API_KEY","DEEPSEEK_... (was (absent))
  ~/.codex/AGENTS.md
    upsert marked rules block

Notes:
  - Codex stdio children do not inherit the parent environment, so the entry forwards DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and every DEEPSEEK_* option variable explicitly via env_vars; shell-set knobs reach the server without hand-editing config.toml.
  - The shared config file needs no forwarding at all: the server reads it itself.
  - Rules block upserted in ~/.codex/AGENTS.md; Codex reads ~/.codex/AGENTS.md plus every AGENTS.md from the project root to the cwd.
  - Shared config ownership is recorded in ~/.codex/.config.toml.deepseek-web-retrieval.codex.owner.json; uninstall releases it. Keep this local metadata with the config.

Plan only — re-run with --apply to write these changes.
```

Repeat your chosen command with `--apply` to write the plan. The host guides explain
activation steps and per-host tier limits. Pi defaults to the extension path; add
`--path mcp` to use its MCP fallback.

Add `--pin` to register the exact version of the CLI you are running
(`deepseek-web-retrieval@<version>`) instead of the unpinned name, so hosts keep
resolving that release rather than every latest publish. The trade-off is no
auto-updates: re-run `init --pin` from a newer CLI to move the pin.

Other stdio MCP hosts may use the server, but the supported setup guides and installer
currently cover the four hosts above. See the [integration model](docs/integration.md)
for tested versions and the [control tiers](docs/research/control-matrix.md) for
routing limits. For an existing installation, follow the
[upgrade instructions](docs/integration.md#upgrading-existing-installs).

## General behavior

What this adapter layer adds on top of the
[DeepSeek Search and Fetch APIs](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/search) — the APIs'
own capabilities (Markdown-only output, no JavaScript rendering, no private networks or
binary files, per-request billing) are documented there.

| Setting | Default | Knob |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Results per search | 10 | `count` |
| Fetch output cap | 16,000 characters | `fetchMaxChars` |
| Search summary cap | 1,200 characters | `maxSummaryChars` |
| Inline content cap, per result (when requested) | 1,500 characters | `searchContentMaxChars` |
| Request timeout, body read included | 30 s (60 s for `need_content` calls) | `searchTimeoutMs` / `fetchTimeoutMs` / `searchContentTimeoutMs` |
| Transient retries | 2 (range 0–5) | `maxRetries` |

### Search

- Requests summaries by default (`need_content: false`, falling back from `summary` to
  `snippet`); a summary the cap shortens ends with an ellipsis. When a call sets
  `need_content: true`, each result instead carries its page body as Markdown, clamped
  to `searchContentMaxChars` per result — a missing body falls back to the summary.
- Deduplicates URLs; an empty result set is normal, not an error.
- Builds `blockedDomains`, `includeDomains`, and `language` into query operators (part of
  DeepSeek's documented search syntax). A combined query over the API's 128-character limit
  degrades instead of failing — the query body truncates first, the language filter drops
  next, the include list last, and blocked domains never drop — and whenever operators or
  degradation changed the query, the result text opens with `Searched for: <effective query>`
  so the model can attribute what it sees.
- Optional `rerank_score` and `authority` thresholds are off by default — the default
  returns exactly what DeepSeek ranked. A positive threshold drops results below it.
  A missing `rerank_score` is dropped too; an unknown `authority` stays unless
  `allowUnknownAuthority` is set to false.
- On the paths where this package defines the search tool's inputs (the MCP server and
  the Pi extension), the tool accepts an optional `original_question`: the user's
  question in their own words. It is forwarded as DeepSeek's `ori_question`, trimmed
  and truncated to 128 characters; on the Pi extension, a blank input falls back to the
  most recent user message in the session.
- The same paths also take an optional per-call `count` (1–50), overriding the
  configured result count for that one call, and an optional per-call `need_content`
  boolean requesting page bodies in the results (see
  [search content design](docs/design/search-content-design.md)).

### Fetch

- Output is capped per the table above, title included; a `[content truncated]` marker
  is added when the limit leaves room for it. An optional per-call `maxChars` parameter
  (0–1,000,000) on every adapter overrides the configured cap for one call — a model that
  sees the marker can widen the budget and re-fetch.
- A page that already opens with its title as a top-level heading does not get a
  duplicate title.
- URLs must be absolute `http://` or `https://`, credential-free, and at most 8,192
  characters; responses larger than 5 MiB are rejected before parsing.
- `format: "text"` and `format: "html"` are rejected rather than misrepresented.
- Allowed/blocked domain lists and private-host blocking are enforced on the client,
  before a request leaves the machine.

### Timeouts and retries

Request timeouts include reading the response body. Transient failures are retried per
the table; retryable responses are 408, 425, 429, and 5xx, and `Retry-After` is honored
up to 10 seconds. Other failures — including 401, timeouts, and network errors — fail
without retrying.

### No automatic fallback

If no API key is available, Search and Fetch fail. If DeepSeek is unavailable, returns
an error, or times out, the request fails. The tool does not silently switch to another
search provider or fetch implementation.

### Privacy and cost

Queries and URLs are sent to `https://api.deepseek.com`; the API key is sent only as a
Bearer token to DeepSeek and to nothing else. Retrieval is billed per successful request —
see the official docs for pricing and rate limits before enabling a team deployment.

## Configuration

Every knob resolves through one chain, low → high, identically on every host:

`built-in defaults < shared config file < DEEPSEEK_* environment < host-native config`

A higher layer always wins, so nothing already configured loses effect.

The shared file works on every host and takes camelCase keys:
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/deepseek-web-retrieval/config.json` — by default
`~/.config/deepseek-web-retrieval/config.json` on Linux and macOS and
`%APPDATA%\deepseek-web-retrieval\config.json` on Windows.

```json
{
  "count": 20,
  "blockedDomains": ["pinterest.com"],
  "language": "zh",
  "searchLocalization": "203.0.113.7"
}
```

Unknown keys and host-integration keys are warned about on stderr and ignored. The API
key does not go in the file — it keeps its existing channels (`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in the
environment, or OpenCode's stored credential).

Which layer to set for a knob, the full file-key ↔ `DEEPSEEK_*` mapping, per-knob
defaults, and special semantics live in the [configuration guide](docs/configuration.md).
Per-host mechanics — how the environment reaches a stdio server, each host's output caps
and deadlines — live in the host guides: [Codex](docs/agents/codex.md),
[Claude Code](docs/agents/claude-code.md),
[Pi](docs/agents/pi.md), [OpenCode](docs/agents/opencode-v2.md).

To see what actually resolves, run `npx deepseek-web-retrieval config`: every knob
printed with its value and its source (`default`, `file`, or `env`). Problems in the
file or in `DEEPSEEK_*` variables are replayed as visible warnings, and it exits 1 when
there are any — so it doubles as a dotfile CI check. `npx deepseek-web-retrieval config
--search "<query>"` runs one billed search through the effective configuration to verify
the key, config, and network end to end.

## Development

```bash
bun install
bun run check
```

Use `bun run lint:fix` to apply Biome's safe lint fixes and formatting. See
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development checks and e2e scenarios, and
[automated tag releases](CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-releases-maintainers).

The test suite mocks the DeepSeek API and the OpenCode and Pi host APIs; real API calls
require a funded DeepSeek account. Shared retrieval logic lives in `src/core/`; adapters
live in `src/<agent>/` (the cross-host MCP server lives in `src/mcp/`), with adapter docs
in `docs/agents/<agent>.md`.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented here, one sentence per item.

## 0.10.0

- Add `need_content` as an optional per-call boolean on the MCP and Pi search tools: `true` attaches each result's page body as Markdown (structure-preserving, indented into the result list) in place of its summary, and a missing body falls back to the summary; OpenCode's fixed provider input keeps that path summary-only.
- Add the `searchContentMaxChars` (1,500 characters) and `searchContentTimeoutMs` (60,000 ms) deployment knobs — the content envelope every `need_content` call runs inside, never tool parameters, recorded in ADR-0003 and the search content design note.
- State the `need_content` facts — excerpt length, latency, price, and the fetch alternative — in the tool and parameter descriptions, with both full-page routes named side by side, and no usage policy: when content is worth it stays the model's per-call judgment.
- Extend the inline-content research note with the vendor reading that no surveyed architecture couples a content flag to another parameter's value range: budgets are static-range, conditional-effect.
- Add a keyless `pi-mock` e2e leg that drives a real Pi session search with `need_content: true` against the mock upstream and asserts the flag reached the wire and the page body reached the model, with the digest legs now also asserting `need_content: false` by default.

## 0.9.0

- Accept an optional per-call `count` (1–50) on the MCP and Pi search tools and an optional per-call `maxChars` (0–1,000,000) on every adapter's fetch, each overriding the configured value for that one call.
- Open the search result text with `Searched for: <effective query>` whenever domain or language operators — or fitting the query-length limit — changed what was actually searched, so the model can attribute what it sees.
- Degrade gracefully instead of failing when search operators push a combined query past the API's 128-character limit: the query body truncates first, the language filter drops next, the include list last, and blocked domains never drop.
- Align user-facing installer wording with the domain glossary: the secrets refusal and record-repair guidance now say "install record" instead of "state file" or "undo state".
- Add the `baseUrl` knob (`DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL` environment variable or shared-file key) so every retrieval request can be routed through a proxy, enterprise gateway, or mock upstream; only an http(s) URL is accepted and anything else drops back to `https://api.deepseek.com`.
- Add keyless `pi-mock` and `opencode-mock` Docker e2e scenarios that run real host session loops (pi via a custom `models.json` provider, OpenCode via a custom provider) against an in-container mock upstream, invoking both retrieval tools and asserting the tool results reached the model — closing CI's tool-execution blind spot without a billed key — and document the keyless (CI) versus billed (local, real API) e2e responsibilities with a `test:e2e:billed` script.

## 0.8.0

- Add Claude Code as a supported host: an MCP-only integration registered in `.mcp.json` (project scope) or `~/.claude.json` (Claude Code's user scope — global scope in this repo's vocabulary), with a full installer host module (plan/apply/uninstall, both scopes), a `docs/agents/claude-code.md` guide, a version probe with drift note, and managed-policy detection that reports a `managed-settings.json` layer outranking the install.
- Route Claude Code tiers through its own settings files: forced capabilities deny the built-in `WebSearch`/`WebFetch` via `permissions.deny` in `.claude/settings.json` or `~/.claude/settings.json` (merged with the user's entries), off capabilities deny the full `mcp__deepseek__*` tool ids, and preferred writes a rules block into `CLAUDE.md`; web-capable competitor servers are excluded under forced via server-level `mcp__<server>` deny rules instead of refusing the tier.
- Add a billed `claude-code` Docker e2e scenario that runs headless `claude -p` prompts with DeepSeek as the LLM over its Anthropic-compatible endpoint (single key for both legs) and asserts the deny-based kill switch keeps the built-in tools out of the session, plus installer/reinit coverage of the new host in the keyless scenarios.
- Guard Pi's global config files with the shared-file ownership sidecar, and release claims before deleting the install record on uninstall, so two installs under different config homes can no longer claim the same `~/.pi/agent` file.
- Run the Codex and Claude Code version probes through a shell so Windows npm `.cmd` shims launch and the drift check no longer silently skips on Windows.
- Correct the research attribution for Claude Code's MCP `2026-07-28` default negotiation (v2 runtime from 2.1.274+, changelog bullet at 2.1.299 — not 2.1.296).
- Restructure the README around a quickstart and a defaults table, moving the full configuration reference (knob classes, the complete file-key ↔ `DEEPSEEK_*` mapping, special semantics) to a new docs/configuration.md guide.
- Generate the configuration guide's knob table from the config vocabulary itself (`bun run docs:matrix` regenerates it, `--check` fails CI on drift), so the documented key ↔ variable ↔ default mapping can no longer hand-drift from the code.

## 0.7.0

- Layer a shared config file (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/deepseek-web-retrieval/config.json`, camelCase keys) under the environment on every host, with the precedence `built-in defaults < shared file < DEEPSEEK_* environment < host-native config`; unknown and host-integration keys are warned about and ignored, and the API key stays out of the file.
- Add a `config` command that prints every knob with its effective value and source (default, file, or environment — a count-derived `maxResults` is labeled `count`), replays shared-file problems, and verifies the key, config, and network end to end with `config --search "<query>"`.
- Forward every `DEEPSEEK_*` option variable — not just the API key — in the Codex installer's `env_vars` entry, so shell-set knobs reach the stdio server without hand-editing `config.toml`.
- Surface DeepSeek's `rerank_score`, `authority`, and `site_name` on search results in both text and structured output, accept an optional `original_question` on the MCP and Pi search tools (sent as `ori_question`), and add the `searchLocalization` deployment knob.
- Couple `maxResults` to `count` when left unset — configuring only `count` was a silent no-op — and retry transient failures (408/425/429/5xx) twice by default instead of failing the billed call on the first attempt.
- Resolve the shared config directory the Windows way on win32 (`%APPDATA%`, with an explicitly set `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` still winning), for the shared config file and the installer's global records alike.
- Add `init --pin` to register the exact running CLI version (`deepseek-web-retrieval@<version>`) instead of the unpinned name, with package-identity comparisons that still match a pinned ref to its lineage.
- `config` now warns and exits 1 when a `DEEPSEEK_*` variable is set but unusable (unknown name, non-numeric value, no-op switch value) instead of silently showing the default.

## 0.6.0

- Return distinct CLI exit codes — 2 for invalid command lines and 3 when a failed apply could not roll back — and document the codes in the usage text.
- Add a `version` subcommand, record the installer version in install records, and show it in `list` output.
- Route any command-line argument to the installer before the MCP server loads, so installer commands never depend on the server's dependency graph and a mistyped command no longer starts a server.
- Reject duplicate flags instead of silently keeping the last value, and print usage to stderr on a bare invocation.
- Wait up to five minutes for npm's post-upload processing before finalizing automated releases, with retry guidance if processing takes longer.
- Clarify OpenCode and Pi native integration and Codex MCP support across setup, upgrade, security, release, and issue-reporting documentation.

## 0.5.1

- Publish npm packages through GitHub Actions trusted publishing and create GitHub Releases automatically from version tags.
- Gate releases on matching versions and changelog entries, the existing CI matrix, and installation tests of the exact release tarball.

## 0.5.0

- Add a native Pi extension as the default integration, with shared environment configuration and settings-based capability switches.
- Add Pi `--path extension|mcp` and preserve uninstall snapshots when migrating between paths.
- Enforce Pi forced tiers by disabling supported competitors and refusing competitors the host cannot exclude.
- Shape MCP results for each client, including readable text for Codex.
- Use Codex's `disabled_tools` for capability off tiers and report host-version drift during init.
- Keep each capability's preferred rules independent of the other capability's tier.
- Make host SDK peers optional for standalone MCP installs and limit Pi peers to the compatible `^1.3.0` range.
- Reject valued `--apply` flags such as `--apply=false` before writing files.
- Validate install records and refuse corrupt or unreadable records with repair guidance.
- Track shared config ownership to prevent installs from different projects overwriting or uninstalling one another.
- Atomically replace individual files, preserve permissions and symlinks, and serialize conflicting writes with operation locks.
- Verify writes and recovery, reporting `rolled_back` or `recovery_required` when apply fails.
- Preserve user content, original competitor snapshots, and rules separators during re-init and uninstall.
- Use platform-native paths and reject malformed or duplicate rules markers.
- Apply identical Fetch URL validation to string and URL-object inputs.
- Allow unscored search results when `minRerank` is zero while retaining positive-threshold filtering.
- Add injectable retrieval clients so adapter tests no longer replace global `fetch`.
- Remove `formatFetchContent` in favor of `formatFetchedContent`, which also reports truncation.
- Add Biome checks, read-only docs drift detection, and clearer stdio handshake diagnostics.
- Gate releases on full checks, installed-package validation across Node 20/22/24/26 in CI, and keyless Docker regressions.
- Add a published 0.4.0 upgrade regression covering all three hosts, Pi path migration, and restoration of original configuration on uninstall.
- Upgrade existing installs from their original project and scope, selecting `--path mcp` explicitly to retain Pi's MCP path.

# Configuration guide

The one reference for how every knob resolves on every host: the layering
chain, the shared config file, the full knob vocabulary, and which layer to set.
Behavior (what search and fetch do) lives in the README's
[General behavior](../README.md#general-behavior); per-host mechanics (output
caps, deadlines, how the environment reaches a stdio server) live in the host
guides: [Codex](agents/codex.md), [Claude Code](agents/claude-code.md),
[Pi](agents/pi.md),
[OpenCode](agents/opencode-v2.md).

## The resolution chain

Every knob resolves through one chain, low → high, identically on every host:

```text
built-in defaults  <  shared config file  <  DEEPSEEK_* environment  <  host-native config
```

A higher layer always wins, so nothing already configured loses effect. The
host-native layer means OpenCode's plugin options (`opencode.jsonc`), Pi's
`deepseekWebRetrieval` settings namespace, and — for MCP hosts — the per-server
`env` block in the host's registration (that block is how an environment
variable arrives, not a fifth layer).

## The shared config file

`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/deepseek-web-retrieval/config.json` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is
set to a non-empty value (this wins on every platform, Windows included); otherwise
`~/.config/deepseek-web-retrieval/config.json` on Linux and macOS and
`%APPDATA%\deepseek-web-retrieval\config.json` on Windows. camelCase keys:

```json
{
  "count": 20,
  "blockedDomains": ["pinterest.com"],
  "language": "zh",
  "searchLocalization": "203.0.113.7"
}
```

Unknown keys and host-integration keys (below) draw a one-line stderr warning
and are otherwise ignored — a bad file never blocks startup. The API key never
goes in the file; it keeps its existing channels (`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in the
environment, or OpenCode's stored credential).

## Knob classes

| Knob class | Shared file | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API behavior — the user↔DeepSeek relationship | yes — that is the point of the file | `count`, `blockedDomains`, `language`, `maxRetries` |
| Host-sensitive — interacts with host output caps and deadlines | carries the safe defaults; a host layer is the recommended override point | `searchTimeoutMs`, `fetchTimeoutMs`, `fetchMaxChars`, `maxSummaryChars`, `searchContentMaxChars`, `searchContentTimeoutMs` |
| Host integration — the host's tool landscape | rejected — warned about and ignored | `searchEnabled`, `setDefaultWebsearch`, `apiKeySource` |

Keep host-independent intent in the shared file; prefer a host layer when a
host-sensitive knob would cross its host's cap or deadline.

## Special semantics

- **`maxResults` follows `count`** when left unset — configure only `count` and
  the cap moves with it. An explicit `maxResults` still caps; `count` never
  follows `maxResults`.
- **Some switches are false-only.** `allowUnknownAuthority`,
  `fetchBlockPrivateHosts`, `searchEnabled`, and `fetchEnabled` are on by
  default; the environment can only turn them off (`false`, `0`, `no`, or
  `off`). The last two have no file key — they are host-integration keys — so
  they exist only as `DEEPSEEK_ENABLE_SEARCH` and `DEEPSEEK_ENABLE_FETCH`.
  Setting any of them to `true` explicitly changes nothing: the default is
  already on.
- **Invalid environment values are dropped** at startup and the default
  applies. `npx deepseek-web-retrieval config` reports every dropped or
  unknown `DEEPSEEK_*` variable as a warning and exits 1, alongside file
  problems.
- **`searchLocalization` must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address**; anything else
  is dropped at option resolution. It is deployment-level configuration, never
  a per-call tool parameter.
- **The content envelope is deployment-level too.** `searchContentMaxChars` and
  `searchContentTimeoutMs` apply only when a call asks for inline page content
  (`need_content: true`, a per-call tool parameter on the MCP server and the Pi
  extension; OpenCode's provider input has no channel for it, so search stays
  summary-only there). They are never tool parameters — the model cannot see
  which host caps its output. `searchContentMaxChars: 0` drops page bodies
  entirely and the summary digest renders.
- **`baseUrl` routes the retrieval API** (`/v1/tools/search` and
  `/v1/tools/fetch` are composed from it). It is infrastructure routing for
  proxies, gateways, and mock upstreams — not a provider switch, and the package
  never falls back to another search service. Only an http(s) URL survives
  resolution (trailing slashes are stripped); anything else drops back to
  `https://api.deepseek.com`.
- **Domains** in the environment are comma-separated; entries that are not
  domains are dropped (and reported by `config`).

# Integration model

[DeepSeek Web Retrieval](../README.md) is not tied to one host. Whether a coding agent can
use it depends on that agent's extension points.

**Research baseline:** the `baseline` field of [hosts.jsonc](hosts.jsonc). This matrix covers
CLI/terminal agents only; IDE and editor extension surfaces are out of scope. Versions are
the latest stable CLI release checked at that baseline unless noted otherwise. `No` means no
documented native provider or override was found in the checked version; several hosts still
ship built-in web tools. MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools can add equivalent tools, but
do not replace built-ins.

## Mechanisms

| Mechanism | Search | Fetch | Requires | Current implementation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native websearch provider | Yes | No | Host plugin API | OpenCode v2 adapter |
| Native tool / fetch override | No | Yes | Host tool API | OpenCode v2 adapter |
| Custom tool plugin | Yes | Yes | Host plugin API | Cline CLI/SDK; no adapter yet |
| Extension API | Yes | Yes | Host extension API | Pi adapter (`src/pi/`) |
| MCP server | Yes | Yes | Host MCP client | Shipped (`src/mcp/`; Pi, Codex, and Claude Code guides) |
| CLI/HTTP wrapper | Yes | Yes | Host can call external tools | Not shipped |

Why the mechanism distinction matters: some agents expose a native websearch provider,
some only let you add tools, and some only support MCP. A "yes" for one mechanism does
not mean the others are supported — the adapter code and docs need to match the
mechanism the host actually provides. MCP is a protocol, not an agent: one possible
transport for hosts that support MCP tools, never a host itself. `Custom tool plugin`
means adding tools; it does not replace a host's built-ins.

## Upgrading existing installs

For an installation managed by `init`:

1. Run `npx deepseek-web-retrieval@latest list` from the original project directory,
   using the same home and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` as the original installation.
2. Run `npx deepseek-web-retrieval@latest init` with the original `--host`, `--scope`,
   `--search`, and `--fetch` values, changing only the settings you intend to change.
   Review the plan and repeat with `--apply`; re-init preserves the original snapshots
   needed for uninstall. A global install can still claim shared configuration from a
   particular project, so keep the original working directory for upgrades.
3. Refresh the package in the host and start or reload a session as described in its
   guide (for Pi's extension path, `pi update --extensions`).

Two init flags change what gets registered. `--pin` pins the host's package to the exact
version being run (`deepseek-web-retrieval@X.Y.Z` in the registration); upgrading a
pinned install therefore means re-running init with the newer CLI, since updating the
CLI alone does not move an independently pinned host package. `--package` overrides the
ref entirely.

When upgrading from 0.4.0, Pi's default changes from MCP to the native extension.
Pass `--path mcp` explicitly to retain MCP, or `--path extension` to migrate; the plan
shows the old path's removals and retains the original uninstall snapshots. OpenCode's
native plugin and Codex's MCP path remain the same. Standalone MCP installs no longer
require OpenCode or Pi SDKs; native adapters use the SDKs provided by their hosts.

Keep install records and ownership sidecars (the `.owner.json` claim files the installer
writes beside shared config files): deleting them loses recovery information
and can cause a later init to refuse an existing registration. If an operation was
interrupted, follow the [recovery guidance](design/installer-design.md#persistence-and-concurrent-operations)
before retrying. For manual installations, update the package reference or checkout and
follow the host guide rather than adopting the config through init.

# Refuse drift between plan and apply

Status: Accepted — shipped in 0.3.0 (see [CHANGELOG](../../CHANGELOG.md)).

The installer's plan previews the previous value each `set` op replaces, and the
install record must snapshot exactly that value for uninstall to restore. We
decided that apply re-verifies that the current value at every `set` path still
equals the plan-time `previous`, refuses with guidance when it does not
("config changed since the plan was rendered — re-run"), and records the
plan-time snapshot — so the preview, the secret guard, and the record all
describe one snapshot taken once, at plan time.

## Considered Options

- **Inherit the plan-time snapshot silently.** Single source, but apply would
  overwrite an edit made between plan review and `--apply` without the user's
  knowledge — violating the [installer's first
  principle](../design/installer-design.md#principles).
- **Keep re-deriving `previous` at write time** (previous status quo). The
  preview and the record can disagree, and the secret guard (the
  `withSecretGuard` wrapper in `src/installer/hosts/index.ts`), which checks the
  plan-time value, no longer covers what is actually recorded.

## Consequences

A legitimate user edit between plan and apply costs one re-run of `init`. In
exchange, "never overwrite user configuration without the user's knowledge"
holds unconditionally, including the window between plan review and apply.

The record's snapshots are re-derived at apply time rather than copied from the
plan; because the drift check runs immediately before, the two are provably
equal, so the record does describe the plan-time snapshot without a separate
copy step.

# Share one config base layer across hosts

Status: Accepted — shipped in 0.7.0 (see [CHANGELOG](../../CHANGELOG.md)).

The option pipeline was single-sourced — names, defaults, and clamping resolved through
one chain (`src/core/constants.ts` → `src/core/env.ts` → `src/core/options.ts`) — but the
channels feeding it were per
host: `DEEPSEEK_*` shell variables on Pi, only `ctx.options` on OpenCode, and
on Codex only the names the installer's `env_vars` entry forwards — just
`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, so every other knob set in the shell silently never
reached the server. One intent ("20 results, block pinterest.com") took up to
three configuration acts in two vocabularies. We decided that a shared config
file becomes the base layer under every existing channel, with the precedence
`built-in defaults < shared config file < DEEPSEEK_* environment < host-native
config`, a three-class parameter taxonomy that isolates host integration in
the host-native layer and rejects it from the file, and no API key in the
file — auth keeps its existing channels.

## Considered Options

- **Unify on the file alone** (retire the environment and host-option
  vocabularies so there is one configuration act). But host integration —
  `searchEnabled`/`fetchEnabled`, `setDefaultWebsearch`,
  `fetchOverrideWebfetch`, `fetchRegisterTool`, `apiKeySource` — describes the
  host's tool landscape, not the user↔DeepSeek relationship, so the host layer
  must keep owning it, and retiring `DEEPSEEK_*` would break every existing
  shell profile.
- **Keep the per-host channels as the only surface** (previous status quo).
  The Codex `env_vars` trap stays — knobs set in the shell reach the server
  only by hand-editing `config.toml` — and the same knob keeps two
  vocabularies across hosts.

## Consequences

One file — `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/deepseek-web-retrieval/config.json`, default
`~/.config/deepseek-web-retrieval/config.json`, camelCase keys — configures
every host, and host layers keep winning: installer-written intent and
explicit per-host overrides always outrank the base, bounding the blast
radius of a bad shared value. Unknown keys and host-integration keys in the
file draw a one-line stderr warning and are otherwise ignored. Because a bad
shared value now fails everywhere at once, every adapter prints a
deviations-from-defaults summary of its effective configuration.

The installer's Codex `env_vars` entry forwards every `DEEPSEEK_*` name, so
environment overrides work on Codex without hand-editing `config.toml`.
Design detail (per-adapter composition, validation, visibility, rollout)
lives in the [layering design note](../design/config-layering-design.md).

# Expose need_content as the agent's per-call boolean

Status: Accepted — shipped in 0.10.0 (see [CHANGELOG](../../CHANGELOG.md)).

DeepSeek's Search API accepts a `need_content` boolean — return each result's page body —
that this repo had hardcoded `false` since the first release: the wire field arrived, the
pipeline dropped it, and no search result ever carried a page body
([search-inline-content.md](../research/search-inline-content.md)). The same research
pinned why the value cannot travel alone: DeepSeek documents no size bound for the
returned content, host output caps run as tight as Pi's 20 KB MCP-path truncation, and
the 30 s default search timeout does not budget for a server-side page crawl. We decided
that the boolean itself becomes a per-call tool parameter on the model-facing surfaces
(the MCP server and the Pi extension), defaulting to `false`, while the deployment owns
two envelope-only knobs that apply whenever content flows: `searchContentMaxChars` (the
per-result body budget, default 1,500) and `searchContentTimeoutMs` (the timeout a
content call runs on, default 60 s). Neither knob is ever a tool parameter — the model
cannot see which host caps its output, so it cannot own a budget.

## Considered Options

- **A tristate `searchContent: off | on | auto` config mode** gating whether the
  parameter is exposed. The wire value is a boolean; `auto` is invented vocabulary, and
  no per-call parameter in this repo (`count`, fetch `maxChars`) is mode-gated. The
  `on` state's only real beneficiary is OpenCode, whose `websearch` provider input the
  host fixes to `query` — the same upstream gap that already blocks per-call `count`
  ([opencode-v2.md](../agents/opencode-v2.md)).
- **Default-on inline content** (Jina's architecture). DeepSeek documents no size bound
  for `content`; a default `count=10` response at typical page sizes runs 30–110 KB
  against host caps that truncate near 20 KB, and per-request billing makes the call
  free, not the context bloat.
- **The previous status quo** (hardcoded `false`). An agent that needs page bodies must
  guess from summaries which URLs to fetch; a wrong guess is a silent miss.

## Consequences

The model decides per call whether a search carries page bodies — one round-trip
replaces search-plus-fetch when recall matters, and summaries stay the default when
they suffice. A page body replaces its result's digest, clamped to
`searchContentMaxChars` with an ellipsis marker, so a response's content volume is
bounded by budget × count and can never blow a host cap by an undocumented server-side
size. The text channel renders bodies as indented Markdown that keeps heading and list
structure; digests stay one-line. `searchContentMaxChars: 0` drops bodies entirely (the
digest renders) — a deployment kill switch that still pays the slower call, so leaving
the parameter false is the better tool for the model. A result whose content comes back
empty — the API documents per-result absence — falls back to its summary, so a content
call degrades to today's output rather than to nothing. OpenCode stays summary-only
until its provider input widens upstream. Design detail (budget arithmetic, rendering,
per-adapter composition) lives in the
[search content design note](../design/search-content-design.md).

[the compatibility research](../research/mcp-compatibility.md)).

- A `deepseek_web_search` tool backed by DeepSeek Search
- A `deepseek_fetch` tool backed by DeepSeek Fetch

The tools appear in Claude Code as `mcp__deepseek__deepseek_web_search` and
`mcp__deepseek__deepseek_fetch`. Claude Code's built-in `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` tools
are not replaced; see [Control tiers](#control-tiers) for routing them away.

For shared search/fetch limits, retries, and privacy behavior, see
[General behavior](../../README.md#general-behavior).

## Requirements

- Claude Code at the tested version in [`docs/hosts.jsonc`](../hosts.jsonc); init reports
  version drift, and newer versions may require rechecking routing behavior
- Node.js 20 or newer (`npx` runs the server)
- A DeepSeek account with access to `/v1/tools/search` and `/v1/tools/fetch`
- A funded DeepSeek account; Search and Fetch are billed per successful request
- `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` set in the shell that launches Claude Code

## Install

The quickest option is the installer CLI:

```bash
npx deepseek-web-retrieval init --host claude-code --scope project \
  --search <optional|preferred|forced|off> --fetch <optional|preferred|forced|off>
```

It prints the full plan — every file, old value → new value, and notes about existing MCP
servers — and writes nothing until you pass `--apply`. Add `--pin` to register the exact
version of the CLI you are running instead of the always-latest package name. `uninstall`
removes recorded additions and restores snapshotted values that have not since been edited.

`--scope project` registers the server in `./.mcp.json` (shareable via VCS) and writes tier
artifacts to `./.claude/settings.json` and `./CLAUDE.md`; `--scope global` uses

scopes use disjoint files, so both can coexist. An `off` capability is written as the
tool's full id in the `permissions.deny` array — Claude Code's own mechanism, which removes
the tool from the model's context while the server keeps running — merging with any entries
you put there yourself.

When `claude` is on PATH, `init` also probes `claude --version` and
adds a plan note when the installed release differs from the tested lock (see
[hosts.jsonc](../hosts.jsonc)) — version-anchored behavior such as the deny rules may have
drifted between the two.

For an existing installer-managed setup, follow the
[upgrade instructions](../integration.md#upgrading-existing-installs) from the original
project directory and scope.

## Control tiers

Claude Code ships built-in `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` tools; neither is replaceable, so
both capabilities use exclusion for the forced tier:

| Capability | Optional | Preferred | Forced |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Search | Tools registered; the built-in `WebSearch` stays available | Plus a CLAUDE.md rules block steering the model to `mcp__deepseek__deepseek_web_search` | Exclusion: `permissions.deny: ["WebSearch"]` |
| Fetch | Tools registered; the built-in `WebFetch` stays available | Plus the rules block | Exclusion: `permissions.deny: ["WebFetch"]` |

The installer maps each tier to these artifacts. Deny entries land in
`~/.claude/settings.json` (user) or `./.claude/settings.json` (project) and merge with
your existing `permissions.deny` entries. The CLAUDE.md rules block lands in
`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (user) or `./CLAUDE.md` (project); Claude Code loads the user file
plus every CLAUDE.md from the cwd up the directory tree, concatenating the levels — so
the block steers wherever it is installed. Under a forced tier, other web-capable MCP
servers detected in the config are denied by server-level rules (`mcp__<server>` denies
every tool of that server), so routing stays exclusive.

> [!WARNING]
> Deny rules outrank allow rules at every settings level and **cannot be carved out** —
> denying `WebSearch` or `WebFetch` removes the tool for every workflow in the install's
> scope (every project on the machine for `--scope global`). A managed policy layer
> (`managed-settings.json`) outranks both files; the installer reports when one exists.

## Authentication

`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is the only source; MCP has no host credential store. It is forwarded
through the server's `env` block as `${DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}` and read per request, sent only
to `api.deepseek.com` as a Bearer token. Without it the server exits at startup with a
message on stderr.

## Usage

Ask naturally:

```text
Search the web for the latest Claude Code MCP config changes and cite the sources.
Fetch https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp and summarize the config keys.
```

The model calls `mcp__deepseek__deepseek_web_search` or `mcp__deepseek__deepseek_fetch`.

The search tool accepts an optional `original_question` argument — the user's question in
their own words — forwarded as DeepSeek's `ori_question` to sharpen search intent; omit it
when the query already stands alone. It also takes an optional `count` (1–50) for the call,
and the fetch tool takes an optional `maxChars` (0–1,000,000) per-call output budget; each
overrides the configured default for that call, so the model can widen a truncated fetch or
ask for more results without rephrasing the query. When configured domain or language
operators change the query actually sent, the result text opens with
`Searched for: <effective query>` (plus any degradation applied to fit the API's
128-character limit), so the model can attribute results to the configuration in effect.

Tool output is capped at 25k tokens by default (`MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, a Claude Code
environment setting), and successful
text results longer than 50,000 characters are saved to a file and referenced — not
dropped silently.

> sits under the environment layer and works with no env forwarding at all: the server

## Troubleshooting

| Error or symptom | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Server fails to start or `HTTP 401` from the tools | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` must be set in the environment that launches Claude Code; the `${DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}` expansion in the server's `env` block reads it at launch. |
| Project tools missing after install | Claude Code asks once per project whether to use `.mcp.json` servers; approve the `deepseek` server when prompted or via the `/mcp` menu. |
| Both tools missing after startup | At least one of `DEEPSEEK_ENABLE_SEARCH`/`DEEPSEEK_ENABLE_FETCH` must stay enabled; the server exits when both are false. |
| Forced tier still shows the built-in tool | The kill switch is the bare deny rule in `permissions.deny` at the install's scope; a managed policy layer (`managed-settings.json`) outranks it — the plan reports when one exists. |
| Routing not exclusive | Other MCP servers stay registered and are noted in the plan. Under a forced tier, web-capable servers detected in the config (and the other scope's file) are denied by server-level `mcp__<server>` rules; a server added after install is not covered — re-run init. |
| Fetch results appear as a file reference instead of content | Tool output is capped at 25k tokens by default; raise `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` or lower `DEEPSEEK_FETCH_MAX_CHARS`. |
| `HTTP 402`, `HTTP 429` | Top up the DeepSeek account; wait, reduce concurrency, or set `DEEPSEEK_MAX_RETRIES`. |
| Fetch fails on localhost or an internal URL | Use a local fetch tool; DeepSeek cannot reach private networks. |

## Troubleshooting

| Error or symptom | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Server fails to start or `HTTP 401` from the tools | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` must be set in the shell that launches Codex and forwarded via `env_vars`; stdio children do not inherit the environment. |
| Both tools missing after startup | At least one of `DEEPSEEK_ENABLE_SEARCH`/`DEEPSEEK_ENABLE_FETCH` must stay enabled; the server exits when both are false. |
| Search still uses the built-in tool under the forced tier | The kill switch is the top-level `web_search = "disabled"` key; the `[tools] web_search` form is a no-op at 0.163.0. |
| Tool results look like raw JSON | The server omits `structuredContent` for Codex's `codex-mcp-client` client identity so the model reads Markdown; if JSON still appears, a newer Codex renamed the identity — report it. |
| Tools time out before the configured DeepSeek timeout | Codex's per-server `tool_timeout_sec` defaults to 300 s — above the 120 s `DEEPSEEK_*_TIMEOUT_MS` maximum — so this only happens if you lowered it; raise it back above the DeepSeek timeout. |
| Routing not exclusive | Other `[mcp_servers.*]` entries stay registered and are noted in the plan. Under a forced tier, an entry that looks web-capable makes `init` refuse — Codex has no per-server kill switch, so remove the server or restrict its tools via `disabled_tools` by hand. |
| `HTTP 402`, `HTTP 429` | Top up the DeepSeek account; wait, reduce concurrency, or set `DEEPSEEK_MAX_RETRIES`. |
| Fetch fails on localhost or an internal URL | Use a local fetch tool; DeepSeek cannot reach private networks. |

# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments` for reading; add `--json body,labels,comments` (with `--jq` to project fields) when scripting.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`

Infer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Maintainers only: set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; the `/triage` skill reads this flag.)_

When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). Read the resulting block count from the issue's REST representation — `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate; `gh issue view --json` does not expose this field). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0` read as above, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.
- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer to the map's Decisions-so-far (link the resolved child; include the gist URL if the resolving session created one).

# OpenCode v2

OpenCode v2 adapter for [DeepSeek Web Retrieval](../../README.md).

Integration mechanism: OpenCode's native plugin API (`@opencode/plugin`), not MCP.

When loaded, it adds:

- A `websearch` provider with the id `deepseek`
- A `deepseek_fetch` tool backed by DeepSeek Fetch
- An optional drop-in replacement for the built-in `webfetch`

The built-in `webfetch` is not replaced by default. Set `fetchOverrideWebfetch` to `true`
if you want all Markdown fetches to go through DeepSeek.

For shared search/fetch limits, retries, and privacy behavior, see
[General behavior](../../README.md#general-behavior).
For configuration layers, the full knob mapping, and defaults, see the
[configuration guide](../configuration.md).

## Requirements

- OpenCode v2 with `@opencode/plugin` in the `^2.0.32` peer range; the tested version
  is recorded in [`docs/hosts.jsonc`](../hosts.jsonc)
- Node.js 20 or newer and npm when using the installer CLI
- A DeepSeek account with access to `/v1/tools/search` and `/v1/tools/fetch`
- A funded DeepSeek account; Search and Fetch are billed per successful request
- A DeepSeek credential stored in OpenCode, or `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`
- Bun, which OpenCode provides at runtime

No build step is required. OpenCode loads the TypeScript entry point directly.

## Install

The quickest option is the installer CLI:

```bash
npx deepseek-web-retrieval init --host opencode --scope <project|global> \
  --search <optional|forced|off> --fetch <optional|preferred|forced|off>
```

It prints the full plan — every file, old value → new value — and writes nothing until
you pass `--apply`. Add `--pin` to register the exact version of the CLI you are running
instead of the always-latest package name. It snapshots the current `websearch.provider`
before the forced tier replaces it, merges `permissions` without touching yours,
preserves comments in `opencode.jsonc`, and `uninstall` restores recorded values that
have not since been edited.

> [!NOTE]
> Search has no `preferred` tier on OpenCode: the provider is host-level config, never
> a model choice, so the CLI rejects it.

### OpenCode CLI install

The next option is the OpenCode CLI:

```bash
opencode plugin add github:gwokhou/deepseek-web-retrieval
```

This fetches the package into OpenCode's plugin cache and adds a
`"github:gwokhou/deepseek-web-retrieval"` entry to the global `opencode.jsonc`. OpenCode
watches the config and reloads plugins when it changes, so a restart is normally
unnecessary; run `opencode service restart` only if the plugin does not appear.

> [!NOTE]
> `plugin add` registers the `deepseek` websearch provider and the `deepseek_fetch` tool,
> but it does not select them. Search still uses the built-in provider, and the built-in
> `webfetch` stays untouched. To route search through DeepSeek, set `websearch.provider` to
> `deepseek` (see the complete config below), or enable `setDefaultWebsearch` in the plugin
> options.

To replace `webfetch` or change options, replace the string entry with the object form and
edit its `options`:

```jsonc
"plugins": [
  {
    "package": "github:gwokhou/deepseek-web-retrieval",
    "options": { "fetchOverrideWebfetch": true }
  }
]
```

A complete global config:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "github:gwokhou/deepseek-web-retrieval",
      "options": { "fetchOverrideWebfetch": true }
    }
  ],
  "websearch": { "provider": "deepseek" },
  "permissions": [
    { "action": "websearch", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
    { "action": "webfetch", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
    { "action": "deepseek_fetch", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" }
  ]
}
```

### Other install methods

**Published npm package**

Use the bare package name (optionally pinned) as the `package` value:

```jsonc
"plugins": [{ "package": "deepseek-web-retrieval" }]
```

Append `@X.Y.Z` to pin a published version. For an existing installer-managed setup,
follow the [upgrade instructions](../integration.md#upgrading-existing-installs).

**Global checkout**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/guokhou/deepseek-web-retrieval.git \
  ~/.config/opencode/vendor/deepseek-web-retrieval
```

Use `"package": "./vendor/deepseek-web-retrieval"`. On Windows the global config root is
`%APPDATA%\opencode\` (unless `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is explicitly set), so clone into
`%APPDATA%\opencode\vendor\deepseek-web-retrieval` there — the same root the installer
writes to.

**Project checkout**

```bash
mkdir -p .opencode/vendor
git clone https://github.com/gwokhou/deepseek-web-retrieval.git \
  .opencode/vendor/deepseek-web-retrieval
```

Use `"package": "./.opencode/vendor/deepseek-web-retrieval"`.

**Auto-discovery**

Clone or copy the repository into `~/.config/opencode/plugins/deepseek-web-retrieval` or
`.opencode/plugins/deepseek-web-retrieval` (on Windows, `%APPDATA%\opencode\plugins\…`).
Auto-discovered plugins do not receive options,
so `webfetch` stays in place; the `deepseek` search provider and `deepseek_fetch` are still
added.

Do not combine auto-discovery with an explicit `plugins` entry for the same directory.

OpenCode reloads plugins when the config or plugin directory changes, so a restart is
normally unnecessary. If a change does not take effect, restart the background server:

```bash
opencode service restart
```

## Authentication

The adapter resolves a key in this order:

1. The active DeepSeek credential stored in OpenCode
2. `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`

Store a key with `opencode auth login` and choose DeepSeek, or set
`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. `apiKeySource` can be `"auto"` (default), `"opencode"`, or `"env"`.

The key is resolved for every request and sent only to `api.deepseek.com` as a Bearer
token. It is not written to plugin metadata or logs.

## Usage

Ask naturally:

```text
Search the web for the latest OpenCode v2 plugin API changes and cite the sources.
Fetch https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins and summarize the plugin lifecycle.
```

The model calls `websearch` (provider `deepseek`) or `deepseek_fetch`. When
`fetchOverrideWebfetch` is enabled, Markdown fetches go through `webfetch` instead.

DeepSeek's optional `ori_question` is not sent on this path, and the model cannot request a
per-call result count or inline page content (`need_content`): OpenCode's `websearch` tool
input is fixed to `query` (verified unchanged at `@opencode/schema` 2.1.4, the drift check
above the 2.0.32 lock), so the provider has no channel for either — search stays
summary-only here while the MCP server and the Pi extension expose both parameters. Upstream requests:
[anomalyco/opencode#58635](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/58635) (session linkage)
and [#58636](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/58636) (per-call `count`); see the
[research note](../research/ori-question-sourcing.md). The fetch tools are not constrained:
they accept an optional per-call `maxChars` (0–1,000,000) that overrides the configured
`fetchMaxChars` for one call, so the model can widen the budget after seeing a
`[content truncated]` marker. The effective-query header and query degradation notes have no
channel on this path either — OpenCode's result shape is closed — but degradation still runs,
and a query that exceeds the length limit and cannot be degraded further surfaces as an
error.

| --- | --- |
| `DeepSeek API key is not configured` | Run `opencode auth login` or set `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. |
| `HTTP 401, invalid API key` | Check the key and its access to the tools endpoints. |
| `HTTP 402, insufficient balance` | Top up the DeepSeek account. |
| `HTTP 429, rate limited` | Wait, reduce concurrency, or increase `maxRetries`. |
| Search query too long | Shorten the query or reduce configured domain/language operators. |

| Response too large | Use another fetch tool for the full response. |
| `websearch` shows a generic "Unable to search" | Check the OpenCode log for the underlying DeepSeek error. |
| Install or config change does not take effect | Run `opencode service restart`; OpenCode normally reloads plugins automatically. |

```bash
opencode service restart
```

The CLI installs into OpenCode's plugin cache (for example `~/.cache/opencode/npm/` on
Linux). Leaving it is safe; OpenCode re-fetches it if you install again.

# Pi

Pi adapter for [DeepSeek Web Retrieval](../../README.md).

Integration mechanism: Pi's native extension API — the package's `pi` manifest names
`src/pi/extension.ts`, and Pi loads it in-process (via jiti, TypeScript directly) at session
start. The same build also ships an MCP server over stdio as the fallback path
([below](#the-mcp-fallback-path)); the extension is the recommended one:

- The tools are declared to the model like built-ins (`exposure: "direct"` is Pi's own
  default for extension tools — the MCP path defaults its tools to
  `exposure: "codemode"`, which hides them from the model unless the entry opts into
  `direct`; that trap does not exist here).
- Results bypass Pi's MCP layer entirely: no 20 KB middle truncation and no 60 s
  per-request timeout; the adapter's own output cap is the only limit.
- The key is read from the Pi process environment — no `env` forwarding, no `${VAR}`
  indirection in any config file.

When loaded, it adds:

- A `deepseek_web_search` tool backed by DeepSeek Search
- A `deepseek_fetch` tool backed by DeepSeek Fetch

Pi 1.3.0 ships no built-in web tool, so the registered tools are the only web path (see
[Control tiers](#control-tiers)). For
shared search/fetch limits, retries, and privacy behavior, see
[General behavior](../../README.md#general-behavior).
For configuration layers, the full knob mapping, and defaults, see the
[configuration guide](../configuration.md).

## Requirements

- Pi with host SDKs in the `^1.3.0` peer range (`>=1.3.0 <2.0.0`); the tested
  version is recorded in [`docs/hosts.jsonc`](../hosts.jsonc)
- Node.js 20 or newer and npm when using the installer CLI or MCP fallback
- A DeepSeek account with access to `/v1/tools/search` and `/v1/tools/fetch`
- A funded DeepSeek account; Search and Fetch are billed per successful request
- `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` set in the shell that launches Pi

## Install

The quickest option is the installer CLI:

```bash
npx deepseek-web-retrieval init --host pi --scope <project|global> \
  --search <optional|preferred|forced|off> --fetch <optional|preferred|forced|off>
```

It prints the full plan — every file, old value → new value, and notes about existing
packages and MCP servers — and writes nothing until you pass `--apply`. Add `--pin` to
register the exact version of the CLI you are running instead of the always-latest
package name. The default path is
the extension: the plan appends `npm:deepseek-web-retrieval` to the `packages` array in
`~/.pi/agent/settings.json` (global) or `.pi/settings.json` (project), and Pi resolves the
source at the next session start (the first launch fetches the package from npm;
`pi update --extensions` refreshes it later). An off capability is written into the
`deepseekWebRetrieval` settings namespace the extension reads at load. Pass `--path mcp`
to install the [MCP fallback path](#the-mcp-fallback-path) instead. `uninstall` removes
recorded additions and restores unchanged configuration values from their snapshots.

For upgrades from a 0.4.x or earlier install (MCP was Pi's default path before 0.5.0),
select `--path mcp` explicitly to retain the old path, or use
the extension default to migrate; follow the shared
[upgrade instructions](../integration.md#upgrading-existing-installs).

### Manual install

Use Pi's own installer:

```bash
pi install npm:deepseek-web-retrieval           # ~/.pi/agent/settings.json (user)
pi install --local npm:deepseek-web-retrieval   # .pi/settings.json (project)
```

Pi reads the package's `pi` manifest and loads `src/pi/extension.ts` at session start. No
build step and no config entry beyond the `packages` source are needed.

### Local checkout

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gwokhou/deepseek-web-retrieval.git
```

Then point Pi at the checkout (it is itself a valid package):

```bash
pi install /absolute/path/to/deepseek-web-retrieval
```

The extension entry imports only host-supplied modules (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`,
`@earendil-works/pi-ai`) and the package's own `src/core/`, so a plain clone works.

## Control tiers

Pi 1.3.0 ships no built-in web tool, so the registered tools are the only web path at
every tier — forced is de-facto rather than exclusion:

| Capability | Optional | Preferred | Forced |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Search | Tools registered — already the only web search | Plus an AGENTS.md rules block steering the model to the search tool | De-facto: no built-in competitor; web-capable MCP servers in `mcp.json` are disabled |
| Fetch | Tools registered — already the only web fetch | Plus the rules block | De-facto: same |

The installer maps each tier to these artifacts. The rules block lands in
`~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` (global) or `./AGENTS.md` (project), naming the path's tool
ids (`deepseek_web_search` for the extension, `mcp__deepseek__deepseek_web_search` for
the MCP fallback). Under a forced tier, web-capable MCP servers detected in
`~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` or `.pi/mcp.json` get `enabled: false` (each prior value
snapshotted for uninstall); a web-capable `packages` or `extensions` source in
settings.json cannot be excluded — Pi has no per-package kill switch — so `init`
refuses the tier instead of promising routing it cannot deliver. The `off` tier is the
`deepseekWebRetrieval` settings namespace described under
[Configuration](#configuration).

## Authentication

`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is the only source: the extension runs inside the Pi process and reads
the environment directly, so the key must be set in the shell that launches Pi (MCP's env
forwarding does not apply). It is read per request and sent only to `api.deepseek.com` as a
Bearer token. It is not written to tool output or logs. Without it, the first tool call
returns an error naming the missing variable.

## Usage

Ask naturally:

```text
Search the web for the latest Pi extension API changes and cite the sources.
Fetch https://pi.dev/docs/latest/extensions and summarize the extension lifecycle.
```

The model calls `deepseek_web_search` or `deepseek_fetch` — the same names over both paths;
only the MCP fallback prefixes them with `mcp__deepseek__`.

The search tool accepts an optional `original_question` input — the user's question in their
own words — forwarded as DeepSeek's `ori_question` to sharpen search intent. When the model
leaves it blank, the extension falls back to the most recent user message in the session
(best-effort; truncated to the API's 128-character limit). The MCP fallback path has no
session access, so there a blank input simply omits the parameter. The search tool also
takes an optional `count` (1–50) for the call, and the fetch tool an optional `maxChars`
(0–1,000,000) per-call output budget; each overrides the configured default for that call.
When configured domain or language operators change the query actually sent, the result text
opens with `Searched for: <effective query>` (plus any degradation applied to fit the API's
128-character limit), so the model can attribute results to the configuration in effect.

## Configuration

The runtime config surface is the same `DEEPSEEK_*` environment the MCP server reads
(identical defaults and clamping), set in the shell that launches Pi, plus the
`deepseekWebRetrieval` settings namespace for the off switches (written by the installer;
it outranks the environment and is preserved by Pi's own settings rewrites). Invalid
`DEEPSEEK_*` values are dropped at startup and the shared default applies.

The shared config file (`~/.config/deepseek-web-retrieval/config.json`, camelCase keys —
on Windows, `%APPDATA%\deepseek-web-retrieval\config.json`)
also sits in this surface, layered under the environment, and needs no forwarding on any
path — the extension and the MCP server both read the file themselves. One file therefore
configures every host running this package, with this host's environment and settings
still outranking it. `npx deepseek-web-retrieval config` prints what actually resolves —
each knob's value and source, with file warnings surfaced and `--search "<query>"` running
one billed search through it all.

### Search

The "Config file" column names each key's camelCase twin in the shared config file —

| Env variable | Config file | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_COUNT` | `count` | `10` | Results requested from DeepSeek, 1–50. Billing is per request, not per result. |
| `DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS` | `maxResults` | `10` | Results returned to the model after filtering, 0–50; defaults to `DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_COUNT` when unset. `0` returns no results. |
| `DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_MIN_RERANK` | `minRerank` | `0` | Drop results below this relevance score (0–3); results without a finite score pass at zero and are dropped at a positive threshold. |
| `DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_MIN_AUTHORITY` | `minAuthority` | `0` | Drop known authorities below this tier. Authority is 0–4. |
| `DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_ALLOW_UNKNOWN_AUTHORITY` | `allowUnknownAuthority` | `true` | Keep results whose authority is missing or unknown. Set `false`/`0`/`no`/`off` to drop them. |

## Troubleshooting

| Error or symptom | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `Failed to load extension ... at least one must stay enabled` | Both capabilities are off (env or the `deepseekWebRetrieval` namespace); keep at least one on. |
| Tools never appear | Check that the `packages` entry is present (`pi list`) and that the first launch after install could reach npm; `pi update --extensions` re-fetches. |
| First tool call errors on the key | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` must be set in the shell that launches Pi; the extension reads only the process environment. |
| `HTTP 401, invalid API key` | Check the key and its access to the tools endpoints. |
| `HTTP 402, insufficient balance` | Top up the DeepSeek account. |
| `HTTP 429, rate limited` | Wait, reduce concurrency, or set `DEEPSEEK_MAX_RETRIES`. |
| Search query too long | Shorten the query or reduce configured domain/language operators. |
| Fetch fails on localhost or an internal URL | Use a local fetch tool; DeepSeek cannot reach private networks. |
| Project-scope install does not load | Pi gates project-local files behind project trust; approve the project when prompted (or launch with `--approve`). |
